a.text: A cleric, a scientist, a medic, a government worker, a power plant technician...
Leia, what do you want to be when you grow up?
...You want to join the guards? Isn't that an awfully boring job? Like, you'll have to stand at the entrance to the city and try to keep a straight face when someone tells you a joke.
You'll have to get out of bed before sunrise to start your drills. You'll also have to take a ton of tests, and you'll only become a fully-fledged member after passing all of them.
You're not very tall, you're not in very good shape, and you'd struggle to pass those tests, you know.
I see... So, you want to protect others?
Leia, you have a very grand and lofty ideal.

steps.text: Eastern Columbia Wastelands

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: Stay calm. We won't be able to use the communicator until the next base station. This is a normal phenomenon.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: You didn't break it, nor is it going to get a signal no matter how much you fiddle around with it.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Sure, understood.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: Seems like you haven't been on many field operations since joining Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Yes. Sorry. I lack practical experience, so I'll work harder to make up for it.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: If I remember right, you were one of Laterano's... city guards?

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: A member of the Guards. Defending Laterano is indeed one of my duties.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Er, or rather, was. Now, I'm a Rhodes Island operator.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: You certainly conduct yourself with the air of a guard. I often see you standing lookout on the deck. The others have taken to calling you 'that Laterano guard'.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: I can relate to that sense of vigilance though. There are always lurking threats, even inside the landship.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: And it can be an honor to be known by your duties.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: That's all in the past now... Well, it wasn't that long ago. But still, I prefer to go by Plume.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: That said, I'm not really sure how to introduce myself. After coming to Rhodes Island, I never got put in a permanent squad, nor did I get a welcoming party...

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: The work I do here is also very different from what I did in Laterano, and I've been having trouble adjusting.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: —Watch out!

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: There are snipers nearby. Multiple.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Bandits?

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: Not sure if they're after Rhodes Island, or just wasteland opportunists.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: ...Conventional weaponry, judging from this bolt. Looks like they've had their eyes on this logistics escort mission for quite some time now.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: There aren't many places to bunker down in this terrain, and the enemy snipers won't have much cover, but setting up my crossbow here is still risky.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: I'll protect you. I've received similar training in Laterano, often with squad mates using guns.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: I'll deal with any attackers who try to close the distance.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: Alright. Be careful out there.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: As long as we're exchanging fire at this range, I'm more than confident in my own weapon's specs.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: (Keep moving at high speeds so the enemies can't land a shot.)

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: (Draw their attention away from where Firewatch is hiding.)

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Ngh!

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: (No problem. This guy's knife doesn't have as much reach as my poleaxe. I can safely handle a frontal attack as well.)

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: (Now, create some distance so the enemy snipers won't feel worried about friendly fire.)

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: (When they make their move, Firewatch will lock on to their positions and return fire.)

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: (They're not aiming for me, but at where Firewatch is lying in ambush?)

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Huff... Huff...

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: (I'm burning through my stamina... faster than expected...)

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: (Get it together! I need to cover Firewatch while she repositions.)

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: (––No, that's not right.)

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: (So far, I've done everything exactly by the book, like we trained.)

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: (But if I know these tactics by heart, the other side might too.)

steps.name: Astesia
steps.text: Before discussing possible interference in Rhodes Island's affairs from rival businesses in Columbia, I'd first like to bring up one of the operators involved in this mission—Plume.

steps.name: Astesia
steps.text: I just looked up some records, and she's been going on a few too many field operations recently... Actually, her schedule is already tightly packed through the next month.

steps.name: Astesia
steps.text: I bring this up because although these missions are generally less dangerous, that doesn't mean she's not building up fatigue.

steps.name: Astesia
steps.text: We could be at significant risk were they to be attacked by a mercenary organization during this escort mission.

steps.name: Astesia
steps.text: To be honest, nobody noticed that she, uh, submitted so many assignment requests all at once.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: From what I recall, she was never a fan of taking on missions.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: The last time she went on a mission with Reserve Op Team A6, to rescue Infected children, it was her first field operation. I remember it clearly, because I was the squad leader.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Ha, that's right. Even though everyone's seen her around, not many actually know her code name. Most just call her that Laterano guard on the deck.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: It is what it is though. Who told her not to sign up for missions?

steps.name: Astesia
steps.text: I've tried talking to her before, but she seemed... how to put this... rather aloof?

steps.name: Astesia
steps.text: One night, I saw her standing there staring off into the sky. So I asked if she was interested in giving astrology a try. After all, my divinations have earned even the Doctor's recognition.

steps.name: Astesia
steps.text: Turns out, she didn't even know what astrology is. She listened to my explanation very politely, but didn't seem at all interested.

steps.name: Astesia
steps.text: Alas, what a terrible shock that was.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Oh, she was mumbling some mystical mumbo-jumbo the other day. She got that from you then?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: When she accompanied Backfire to Medical two days ago, she was muttering about 'phases' and 'zeniths' and so on. I wanted to slap her out of it, right on the treatment table.

steps.name: Astesia
steps.text: Hm, she may have missed the point somewhat... but I'm glad she at least remembered the words.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Dr. Gavial, the kids from A6 are afraid to go to Medical for checkups. If you could just work on your bedside manner...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: No can do. If they're afraid of the croc doc, that's THEIR problem. Psychologically speaking.

steps.name: Astesia
steps.text: Speaking of which, did the members of A6 work well with Plume on that one operation you had together?

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Extremely. She's a very well-trained fighter. To be honest, I wish the rest of the team would take orders half as well as she did...

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: And on the way back, she was very enthusiastic about teaching Catapult and Popukar how to write an operation report.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: However, she never offered any of her own opinions until the mission debriefing. If she'd taken initiative during the operation itself, things might've gone even better...

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Maybe she found the members of A6 too unreliable, and didn't dare suggest changing plans in the middle of battle.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: She's too rigid. We're not the army here, and our main advantage comes from our flexibility to adjust to any changes.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Oh right, from what I've heard of other operations, you used to be the leader of a tribe, right? You must've been good at leading large groups... and large fights?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Heh, you spend way too much time rubbing shoulders with the folks in HR.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: But my past's not as simple as that...

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: (Charge forward again, then retreat in the direction of Firewatch.)

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Hah, tricked them.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: Enemy sniper down. Plume, create some distance.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: On it.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: The attackers have been dealt with.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: A job well done.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: You led them towards where I was hiding, not away.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: This threw off their intuitions, confusing them into thinking I was hiding elsewhere.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: When snipers face off in the open wilderness, the moment someone reveals their position with their attention on the wrong spot... they're done for.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: Your quick thinking was both brave and incredibly smart.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Uh... thank you. I was about to apologize for acting on my own though.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: That strategy could've put you at risk, and we didn't agreed on it beforehand.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: I was supposed to cover you, but ended up doing the exact opposite.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: No, I'm very glad that you chose in the moment to put your faith in me and trust my abilities.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Yes, it's something another senior at Rhodes Island taught me before.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: She said she hoped I could trust my companions more, as well as... my own judgment.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: What's wrong? Are you hurt?

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Huff... I'm fine, I probably just pushed myself too hard.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: Head back to the vehicle first and rest then. We'll make our way to the en route safe house ASAP, then report this attack to the Rhodes Island landship.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: Let me help. That weapon of yours might be a bit too heavy for you right now.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Huff... Thanks...

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: But I can handle my own poleaxe. I've trained with it so much that it's basically a part of me.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: I can tell that you're academy-trained.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: You're quick to respond to surprise attacks, take action without hesitation, and can nimbly find cover while in the line of fire of two different snipers.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: But I don't think any academy would teach a poleaxe user to sacrifice the weapon's power and rely on speed.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: You're right, I didn't follow the standard guard training.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: The seniors in my squad privately suggested that I offset my weaknesses by bolstering my strengths, so I incorporated some tricks into my fighting style and barely passed the course.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: A very good tradeoff, if you ask me.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: Have you ever considered taking up a different weapon though?

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Most of the guard forces used poleaxes.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: Hm... Of course, that's your decision to make.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: But since you've already found your personal style, it shouldn't be a problem either way.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: Have you recovered a little?

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: I drank some saline water and already feel a lot better.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: I did make a mistake earlier, which made me burn through my stamina too quickly. I wasn't pacing myself at the start of the fight.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: What you remind me of—from what I'm familiar with at least—is a prey animal that's been hunted day and night. Have you gotten enough rest lately?

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Huh? I don't have anything like that going on.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: As a matter of fact, it feels really fulfilling to have a duty to carry out each and every day.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: Every day?

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Mhm. When I first came to Rhodes Island, I had no idea what I was supposed to be doing. Recently, I realized that I should be taking the initiative to apply for missions.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: While I can more or less understand how you feel...

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: Going on too many field operations is unreasonable. You need rest, and your weapon needs maintenance too.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: Have you even been to the Engineering Department since coming to Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Huh? No, but I think my weapon is in pretty good shape.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: Don't worry, the craftspeople here are familiar with Laterano weapons. There are several masters in the repair shop who can fix even guns with ease.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: They might even be able to give you some ideas on how to upgrade your poleaxe to make it more comfortable.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Good idea. I'll keep that in mind.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Honestly, I've been thinking the same thing. My weapon could use some modifications, since our tasks here are so different from the guard forces.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: Let's get a move on. The sun's starting to set, and we need to reach the safe house before dark.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: And that's a full overview of the field operation. After dispatching the ambushers at the outset, we encountered no other threats.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: The attackers were obviously mercenaries, and I've collected the bolts they used. Unfortunately, this information alone cannot reveal the identity of whoever's behind this.

steps.name: Firewatch
steps.text: I'll leave them here with the report, Doctor. If you have no other questions, I'll take my leave.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: I'll also–

options: Someone from HR wants to talk to you.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Alright... I'm honored that you remember my code name, Doctor.

steps.name: Human Resources Operator
steps.text: Your application to serve as the Doctor's bodyguard has been carefully reviewed.

steps.name: Human Resources Operator
steps.text: Unfortunately, the Doctor has decided that a personal bodyguard is unnecessary while aboard the Rhodes Island landship.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Oh, that's something I sent out earlier...

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Um... Thank you for your time and patience. I'm sorry that my abilities are not up to par...

steps.name: Human Resources Operator
steps.text: Ahem... You don't need to take it that seriously, Plume.

steps.name: Human Resources Operator
steps.text: The good news is that you've been recognized for your performance in recent field missions, and the Doctor will need escorts when conducting operations away from the ship.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: In other words, I got the job?

steps.name: Human Resources Operator
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Human Resources Operator
steps.text: That said, one of our operators reported that you've been applying for an unusually high number of field missions. As HR Department staff, I need to know the reason.

steps.name: Human Resources Operator
steps.text: Although you've been pretty tight-lipped about your past, you did come with those two Laterano operators after all...

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: I don't know what they've been through, nor do I have the right to ask.

steps.name: Human Resources Operator
steps.text: What I'm trying to say is that I've heard a word or two about your pre-Rhodes Island situation from them.

steps.name: Human Resources Operator
steps.text: Uh, the way they put it was that they 'felt bad for you because you seemed so lost and directionless all the time,' which is why they brought you out of Laterano.

steps.name: Human Resources Operator
steps.text: Considering that you still value Laterano glory, but have been dismissed from the guard forces, I would like to confirm your motives for taking on these recent field missions.

steps.name: Human Resources Operator
steps.text: Are you regretting the decision you made at the time?

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: No, I don't regret it... At least not anymore.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: I can trust my own judgment now. In the face of life and death, the rules can be bent.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: And after coming to Rhodes Island, I realized that people with Oripathy don't infect others simply by walking down the street, nor are they just waiting for death to come.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Seeing how Backfire is still alive and conscious, can still participate in training, and can still talk to the captain as energetically as before... It truly makes me happy.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: I've also come to terms with the fact that I can't go back to the Laterano Guards. Rhodes Island and Laterano are completely different places, and I've also had to change.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Plus, I'm really fascinated by the things people talk about here, even if I don't fully understand them.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: In my experience, field missions give me more opportunities to work with my teammates, and should help me better integrate into the group.

steps.name: Human Resources Operator
steps.text: About that... Actually, many operators bond over common interests, such as Pinecone's woodcrafting group, or Vigna's band...

steps.name: Human Resources Operator
steps.text: Speaking of which, they seem to be missing a bass player right now?

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: Mm... Thanks for letting me know. I'll think about it.

steps.name: Plume
steps.text: By the way, Firewatch recommended the 'Vitafield' clothing brand to me. I heard they're currently in a business relationship with us. Can you tell me more about it?

steps.name: Human Resources Operator
steps.text: Eh... Plume?

options: Go ahead and show her around.
I think we're done with the serious stuff.

steps.name: Human Resources Operator
steps.text: Um, alright, if it's fine with you, Doctor. I'll go grab one of my colleagues then.
